speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a young patient presenting with wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions. To understand what is happening, can you tell me how long you have had these symptoms and if they appeared all at once or developed over time?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is helpful; the recent knee pain and Minnesota camping trip are significant clues. Given the monoarticular involvement and travel history, could you describe the appearance of the skin lesions on your wrist and whether you have noticed any eye pain, swelling, or redness in your joints?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Lyme Arthritis (Borrelia burgdorferi infection)
